literal: Blame ceasing those who live indeed they live; fame ceasing those who live indeed those who do not live.
translation: Only those who live without blame truly live. Those who live without fame are as good as dead.
modern: பழி இல்லாமல் வாழ்பவர்களே உண்மையாக வாழ்பவர்கள். புகழ் இல்லாமல் வாழ்பவர்கள் உயிருடன் இருந்தாலும் வாழாதவர்களே ஆவர்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts a life of blame with a life of fame. The word vasai means blame or reproach, and living without it is the mark of true life. Conversely, isai means fame or good reputation. The poet asserts that those who exist without earning a good reputation do not truly live at all, equating a fameless existence to not being alive.
